dedupe_keys.name: open cities ai challenge dataset drone imagery and openstreetmap building footprints african cities

description: The Open Cities AI Challenge, run on DrivenData and completed in March 2020 with 1,099 participants, asked teams to segment building footprints from high-resolution drone imagery to support disaster risk management in African cities. Its data cover 12 African cities and regions and more than 700,000 buildings, with footprints mostly taken from OpenStreetMap and annotated with local OpenStreetMap communities; imagery comes as four-band Cloud Optimized GeoTIFFs catalogued with STAC, and training data are split into more complete tier 1 and less complete tier 2 labels, for example 121,171 tier 1 buildings in Dar es Salaam. The winning model reached a Jaccard score of 0.86 on the private test set, and a Responsible AI track examined ethical issues of AI for disaster risk. Coverage: 12 African cities and regions, including Dar es Salaam, Lusaka and Zanzibar. Access: released for ongoing use by the project team. Licence: ODbL 1.0, as stated on the Source Cooperative product page of the dataset (source.coop/open-cities/ai-challenge); the competition rules ask the winners to release their code under the MIT licence, which is a separate matter. Caveats: label completeness and resolution vary by city. Simulation uses are building footprint extraction for exposure mapping in fast-growing cities. Related records: SpaceNet and the CrowdAI Mapping Challenge dataset.
